extracted.intended_audience: corporate clients, in-house counsel, and litigators involved in or considering US ITC Section 337 investigations
extracted.subtask_description: Representation of complainants or respondents in US International Trade Commission (Section 337) investigations alleging imported products infringe patents, trademarks, or involve unfair competition; includes seeking/executing remedies (exclusion orders, cease-and-desist), managing expedited procedures, and handling appeals and Presidential review. Emphasis on integrated trade, IP, and appellate strategy and rapid fact and document development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter of Section 337 investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 337 investigations typically involve intellectual property rights, including allegations that imported goods have infringed patents (including utility and design patents) and trademarks (whether registered or common law). Companies can also assert other forms of unfair competition involving imported products, including antitrust claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Section 337 for imported-product disputes involving patents, trademarks, and other unfair competition theories; ensure the asserted theory fits within imported goods jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary remedy — exclusion orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary Section 337 remedy is an exclusion order that directs US Customs and Border Protection to block infringing imports from entering the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion orders are a distinctive and powerful remedy available at the ITC (not generally available in federal courts) and are a core reason companies pursue Section 337 investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional remedies — cease-and-desist and temporary relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies may also seek cease-and-desist orders barring the sale of infringing products already imported, as well as expedited relief through temporary exclusion orders and cease-and-desist orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requests for temporary exclusion or temporary cease-and-desist early when immediate relief is needed; evaluate both blocking future imports and stopping domestic sales of existing imports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 337 investigations typically reach a final decision within 16 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and execute discovery, expert development, and trial preparation on an accelerated schedule compared to district court litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for rapid fact/document/witness marshaling
rubrics_metrics.description: We determine, no later than 60 days before the hearing, whether to request a summary determination; participate actively in the trial before the administrative law judge; make public interest, remedy and other submissions during the ITC’s review following the initial determination; lobby relevant government agencies during the Presidential review phase; and appeal, when necessary, to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a compressed project plan: marshal necessary facts, witnesses and documents quickly, decide on motions (including summary determination) on a strict timeline, and be prepared for immediate post-determination processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for summary determination request
rubrics_metrics.description: We determine, no later than 60 days before the hearing, whether to request a summary determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the summary-determination decision early in the pre-hearing schedule so the team can prepare supporting evidence or rebuttal materials under the tight ITC timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active trial participation before the ALJ
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate actively in the trial before the administrative law judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full trial presentation (fact witnesses, expert testimony, demonstratives) before the ALJ; prepare for an intensive, week-long (or multi-week) hearing on an accelerated calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-initial determination submissions and Presidential review engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Make public interest, remedy and other submissions during the ITC’s review following the initial determination; lobby relevant government agencies during the Presidential review phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare persuasive public-interest and remedy submissions; coordinate advocacy with executive-branch stakeholders to influence Presidential review when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate preparedness — Federal Circuit review
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal, when necessary, to the Federal Circuit. The US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has exclusive appellate jurisdiction over the ITC’s Section 337 determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect appeals; ensure appellate counsel and strategy are integrated early because many ITC decisions are appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for large, multi-disciplinary teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases before the ITC move quickly and require a firm that can commit a large team if needed. We can staff and manage such a team swiftly. Our large IP practice, together with our 350‑lawyer litigation department, brings extensive experience litigating patent and trademark disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble sufficient staffing (trial lawyers, technical experts, discovery/forensics, trade counsel, appellate litigators) to meet parallel, compressed tasks and international issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with trade and appellate practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Our IP litigation capabilities are fully integrated with essential counseling support from other practices. Our global trade group contributes extensive experience representing companies before the ITC and Customs in trade remedy matters. Our Supreme Court & Appellate practice provides resources for appeals affecting patent law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate IP litigation with global trade and appellate teams to cover customs enforcement, trade-remedy expertise, and appellate strategy that frequently arise in Section 337 matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: International discovery and global presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Our global footprint gives us the reach and ability to manage the international discovery issues that inevitably arise in Section 337 actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for cross-border discovery, collection and coordination with foreign counsel; staffing in relevant jurisdictions and cultural/legal familiarity can be decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business-focused settlement and resolution strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Our ultimate goal is to resolve disputes in the manner best suited to a client’s particular needs: this can include reaching settlements, when appropriate, via licensing arrangements, joint ventures, mergers and other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate commercial resolution options (licenses, joint ventures, mergers) alongside litigation to maximize client flexibility, protect investments, and increase market share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience and technical expertise across technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Our patent lawyers provide valuable experience and technical knowledge in numerous fields, including medical device technologies, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, chemistry, life sciences, electrical and mechanical engineering, telecommunications, computer hardware and software, and related manufacturing processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match technical experts and counsel to the technology at issue to present effective claim construction, infringement, and validity positions in the ITC context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation diversity — complainants, respondents, and third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: We have represented complainants, respondents and interested third parties in Section 337 investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop tailored strategies depending on role: pursue exclusion and domestic remedy strategies as complainant; seek defenses, sanctions, or stays as respondent; and consider amicus/intervenor posture for third parties.
